guide.title: Behavioral & Psychiatric Emergencies
guide.lead: Never assume behaviour is "just psychiatric": check the glucose, oxygen and temperature first. Keep yourself safe, talk before you touch, and never restrain anyone face down. Ask directly about suicide; asking doesn't plant the idea.

sections.title: Rule out the medical causes
items: Check glucose, SpO₂ and temperature on everyone

steps.title: Scene safety
steps.text: Police if there's a weapon or violence; keep an exit.

steps.title: Talk first
steps.text: One calm speaker, space, listen, acknowledge feelings, offer choices.

steps.title: Hyperactive delirium?
steps.text: Hot, sweating, very strong, stripping clothes, fast pulse: a medical emergency with risk of sudden death.

steps.title: Restraint only if needed
steps.text: Minimal; never prone or with weight on the back or neck.

steps.title: Monitor continuously
steps.text: SpO₂, EtCO₂, breathing; cool if hot.

groups.title: Higher risk
items: Access to lethal means; isolation; recent loss

sections.title: Other situations
items: Psychosis: calm, don't argue with or reinforce delusions, keep distance and an exit
Panic attack is a diagnosis of exclusion: PE, ACS, asthma, anaphylaxis, hypoglycemia first; never a paper bag
Involuntary holds: danger to self, danger to others, or unable to care for self; rules vary by jurisdiction

quiz.q: Agitated man shouting at unseen people, sweating, HR 124, hot, stripping off in the cold; glucose and SpO₂ normal. Highest priority?
options: Hyperactive delirium with possible stimulant use: medical emergency – cool, de-escalate, rapid transport
quiz.explanation: It can progress to sudden cardiac arrest.

quiz.q: A 22-year-old has chest tightness, palpitations, tingling and fear of dying during an exam. Next step?
options: Rule out PE, ACS, asthma and anaphylaxis, then calm reassurance and slow breathing
Lights and sirens for presumed PE
quiz.explanation: Panic is a diagnosis of exclusion.

quiz.q: Police have a sweating, struggling methamphetamine user handcuffed face down. Most important action?
options: Get him onto his side now and monitor breathing and SpO₂
Leave him prone: he's still fighting
Sit on his back to calm him
quiz.explanation: Prone restraint can cause positional asphyxia and sudden death.

quiz.q: First check in any patient with abnormal behaviour:
options: Whether they are known to police

quiz.explanation: Plan and access to means add risk.

quiz.q: Asking directly "Are you thinking about killing yourself?":
options: Is recommended and doesn't plant the idea
quiz.explanation: Then ask about plan, means and intent.

quiz.q: A patient insists the TV is controlling him. You should:
options: Stay calm, acknowledge his fear, not argue or agree
Never prone; on the side or seated, monitored
Prone with weight on the back
quiz.explanation: Continuous SpO₂ and EtCO₂ after sedation.

quiz.q: Grounds for an involuntary hold generally include:
options: Danger to self, to others, or unable to care for self
Refusing treatment for a minor injury
Is no longer used; say hyperactive delirium with severe agitation
quiz.explanation: Treat it as a medical emergency.

flashcards.question: Medical causes to rule out first
flashcards.answer: Hypoglycemia, hypoxia, intoxication or withdrawal, head injury, infection or sepsis, stroke, postictal state, hyperthermia.

flashcards.question: Hyperactive delirium with severe agitation
flashcards.answer: Agitation, hyperthermia, sweating, tachycardia, unusual strength: a medical emergency that can cause sudden death. ("Excited delirium" is no longer used.)

flashcards.question: Restraint safety
flashcards.answer: Never prone or with weight on the back or neck. Side or seated; monitor breathing, SpO₂ and EtCO₂ continuously.

flashcards.question: Assessing suicide risk
flashcards.answer: Ask directly; plan, means, intent, timing; previous attempts, isolation, recent loss.

flashcards.question: Approaching psychosis
flashcards.answer: Calm and respectful; acknowledge feelings; don't argue with or reinforce delusions; keep distance and an exit.

flashcards.question: Panic attack or emergency?
flashcards.answer: Panic is a diagnosis of exclusion: rule out PE, ACS, asthma, anaphylaxis, hypoglycemia.

flashcards.question: Verbal de-escalation
flashcards.answer: One calm speaker, space, listen, acknowledge feelings, offer choices, keep an exit.

flashcards.question: Involuntary holds
flashcards.answer: Danger to self, danger to others, or unable to care for self; criteria vary by jurisdiction.

critical.scenario: A man with paranoid schizophrenia off his medication is shouting that "the government watches me through the lights" in a crowded community centre. The manager asks you to calm him down.
critical.question: Safest initial approach?

options.t: Clear the room, keep a safe distance with an exit, one calm speaker, acknowledge his fear without challenging the delusion, offer choices; police as backup
Approach together and tell him to leave or police will come
Argue that nobody is watching him

critical.explanation: "I can see you're scared. No one here wants to hurt you."
critical.kpi: Applies de-escalation principles in a patient with paranoid psychosis

critical.scenario: A 55-year-old widow living alone says she can't go on and has saved her BP pills to take at once; 30 tablets are in her drawer. She's willing to go to hospital.
critical.question: Priorities?

options.t: High risk: never leave her alone, remove the pills with her permission, constant observation, record her exact words, transport
She's voluntary, so no further action
options.f: Plan and means make her high risk.

options.t: Let her pack alone while you wait outside

critical.explanation: With her consent, involve a trusted contact.
critical.kpi: Recognises high suicide risk and implements safety precautions including constant observation and means removal

critical.scenario: A man with a seizure-disorder bracelet is confused in a parking lot: pupils 1–2 mm, HR 54, RR 8 and shallow, SpO₂ 88%. An unidentified pill lies nearby.
critical.question: Priority?

options.t: Treat the opioid toxidrome: open the airway, ventilate with a BVM and oxygen, naloxone while ventilating, bring the pill
Postictal state: oxygen and routine transport
options.f: Pinpoint pupils and RR 8 point to opioids.

critical.explanation: Treat what you see, not just the history.
critical.kpi: Prioritises presenting toxidrome over medical history when managing altered mental status
